1: Bring Your Feelings to Work Day. A small box, one afternoon, and apparently a shipping crate of stationery.
Someone might actually want to tell us something.
People tell us things already. Then someone puts them on a form and they stop.
Can one of them tell you the west corridor's been whining for three days?
2: Do I have to write a feeling to get into the corridor?
No. The box is voluntary. I can also decline to record your silence.
I'm only keeping the maintenance reports. Nobody's personal life belongs in the same folder.
That's encouraging. I was about to submit a complaint about the box itself.
3: Here. My feeling is that the corridor makes a horrible noise every fourth cycle.
That's a service complaint. We can actually do something with it.
It also sounds extremely personal when you say it that way.
The machine is whining. I'm being polite.
Have someone check the actual machine before anybody starts interpreting the card.
4: There it is again. From behind Berth Three.
I heard it Tuesday. Thought it was the cleaning cart.
I told the cart driver he had a terrible cart.
Good. We've narrowed it down to every moving part in the corridor.
5: Some cards describe feelings, some describe equipment, and one appears to be a restaurant review.
I can test the noise. I can't test whether the cafe deserved one star.
Do we know who left the card?
We shouldn't. That's why the box is anonymous.
I think I recognize the handwriting.
That's exactly what an anonymous box needs. Amateur detectives.
I'll leave the author field empty. The words are enough for the repair.
6: It won't make the noise with the hatch open.
Then close it and run the same cycle as the complaint. I want to hear what they heard.
I like this part of science. The part where we admit the first test didn't prove anything.
You mostly like being allowed to do something twice.
If the second time counts as work, yes.
7: The card says 'during the late cycle.' The maintenance log says we never tested it late.
Then someone was describing a real problem. We made it sound like a mood.
Can we send the specific timing to Zib?
Already did. I didn't include who might've written the card.
Good. It's embarrassing enough when your own coworkers think they can recognize you from a complaint.
8: This card is unmistakably the work of someone with a grievance.
It's an anonymous box. That describes literally everybody.
I don't think that's fair to everybody.
The phrase 'a persistent whine' narrows my suspects.
Don't look at me like that. I only make noise when I'm right.
Put the case away, Brick. Zib has an actual wrench and an actual problem.
9: I wrote the one about people asking if I'm all right.
Oh. I thought you were annoyed about the quiet room.
I like the room. I don't like being told what my water rig must feel like by people who have never worn it.
Quite often. But I like you, so I've been kind about it.
I was going to ask how you are.
You may ask whether the room is warm. Then I'll tell you.
10: It makes the same noise when the return cycle starts.
And not when the hatch is open. We've reproduced the condition.
The coupling vibrates just enough to hit the cover.
I owe the cart driver an apology.
Buy him a replacement wheel and we'll call it even.
11: I'll adjust the coupling. Keep your ear by the cover, not your head inside it.
Silence. I haven't heard that much silence since Kreeb tried the quiet room.
Then it's fixed. Tell Glorp the card was useful. Don't tell Brick it was evidence.
12: The noise complaint is closed. The repair record doesn't include anybody's private card.
That seems fair. They told us enough to find it.
And someone else now gets to walk that corridor without the noise.
That is worth more than knowing who wrote it.
I've kept the equipment trace. It describes the change perfectly well.
13: Central says participation is low and the disclosure categories are incomplete.
The crew came to work. They repaired a real fault. That should count as something.
The lab numbers don't support a relationship between a statement and residue.
They want us to sort private stories into named categories anyway.
People told us things because they trusted us, not because they wanted a scoring system.
14: We have two residue readings, and one of them is too small to interpret.
The maintenance record is more complete than the material record.
Of course. Zib didn't have to discover a new physical phenomenon to tighten a coupling.
15: The anonymous submissions contain several striking omissions.
An omission in an anonymous submission is usually called privacy.
If people want to tell us more, they'll tell us themselves.
That's a surprisingly unsatisfying investigative technique.
It's also the one we're keeping.
16: We'll report the noise repair and the physical observations. Nothing personal.
Say we don't know whether the material readings have anything to do with the cards.
Done. And the author fields stay empty.
You can say the quiet room worked for people who chose it.
I've recorded it as an available space. No attendance roster.
17: Central hasn't accepted the difference between low disclosure and no useful work.
They should visit. They'll hear a station without that terrible whine.
They're sending a liaison. An actual person.
Oh. That's more alarming than the box.
18: We have a visitor next week. I want the route clear and the evidence ready.
I'll check the route. Please don't make me memorize a speech about how lovely the corridors are.
Would you like the tour to include the place we just repaired?
Yes. We actually did something there.
19: You've made a presentation of the service corridor. It has a wall, some pipes, and two doors.
It's also where we fixed a real problem.
Then let them see it. Don't put a velvet rope around the manifold.
I wasn't going to put a velvet rope anywhere.
Good. I hate moving velvet ropes.
20: I've gathered the records that show what we know and what we don't.
Please leave in the failed tests. Those are the ones I can explain honestly.
And no one is giving the liaison copies of anonymous cards.
Should I brief our visitor on the unresolved case of the bright chair?
You may brief the chair. The visitor has enough to do.
21: The visitor's arrival time is confirmed.
I'll check the route from the dock. Last time a guest got lost behind the spare-chair cupboard.
That guest was a delivery driver.
Yes. He stayed for lunch and recommended the vending-machine curry.
I still haven't met anyone who agrees with him.
22: I have identified the author of the anonymous note.
No. You've identified three people who use the word 'whine.'
That's an unusually broad suspect pool.
The sound is fixed, Brick. The case can go home.
